title: metric_relationships
description: Two shapes, one file. The ANSWER a person writes at the X4 gate — `relationships[]`, keyed by metric name — and the ARTIFACT the stage writes back, `edges[]`, already resolved to metric refs and ready for POST /artifacts/metric/{id}/relationships. Both are accepted here because the stage validates the answer with the same schema it validates its own output against, and a drift between the two would be a drift nobody notices.

relationships.description: The answer: one entry per metric that derives from something. A metric that derives from nothing is omitted, not listed empty.

metric.description: The metric's `name`, exactly as the card spells it.
The TARGET metric's name — what this one is derived from.

relation.description: What the relationship IS, in metric terms. The stage maps it to the edge vocabulary — `derivation` and `restriction` write `depends_on`, the other two write no edge and go to the cards' `definition.extensions.related`, because `metric` declares no `alternative` — and carries this word itself in the edge's attributes, because `depends_on` is the same name for a ratio's numerator and for a narrowed population.

role.description: What the target plays: numerator, denominator or component on a derivation, base on a restriction. Refused on a grain_variant or an alternative, which have no roles.

why.description: What the target CONTRIBUTES, in a sentence a reader can check against the two SQL bodies. An edge nobody can check is worse than no edge.

exact.description: True when the populations nest — every row the target counts is a row this metric counts, or the composition is arithmetically exact. Default true.

differs.description: Required when `exact` is false: what does NOT line up. A consumer dividing one of these by the other needs this sentence.

label.description: Free prose carried onto the graph edge itself.

edges.description: The stage's own output: one resolved edge per assertion, in the shape POST .../relationships takes.

rel_type.description: The edge type, derived from `relation`: `depends_on` or `alternative`. Never invented: an unknown type would be known to no reader.

attributes.description: Carried onto the edge verbatim and read by nothing structurally: it is where the reasoning goes.

relation.description: The metric-domain relation this edge was asserted as.
